description:
## Current delivery contract — user-approved two-outcome stack
Owner: PR B. One PR per complete outcome, NOT one PR per bead. Keep detailed beads and cohesive internal commits for tracking; consolidate existing draft foundations into their owning feature PR where practical. PR B stacks on independently usable PR A. Include owning PR documentation and validation there. This supersedes earlier per-bead/prerequisite PR instructions and historical comments. Closed foundation status is not outcome acceptance.
New-feature E2E requires explicit human UX approval in zaq-emb.32; no self-approval.

PR B integration seam split from .4: bind requests to resolved Person and authorized canonical transcript; reuse existing history loader/accounts.fetch_history/admission/finalization rather than duplicate Actions. Wire private execution records and initial authorized hydration; preserve BO session identity and connector-scoped channel resolution. Validate current request handle versus registered identity. Busy/finalizing requests must be accepted/steered with explicit outcome or explicitly rejected, never silently lost or marked answered. Tests FIRST: nil/forged actor denial, revoked history, authorized initial hydration, exact active request/runtime identity, busy/finalizing races, one public answer owner and execution-private data exclusion. Files: IncomingMessageRouter, Agent history loader/tools/executor and Engine execution APIs. Read Agent critical checks, Engine guide, Action reuse/testing policies. Cross-service calls through NodeRouter. No PR A dependency on this work; deliver in B, not its own PR.

## Alignment update — 2026-10-07 / a0c8796e
Supersedes stale baseline/file-reservation instructions. Durable packages: zaq-emb.30.1, zaq-emb.30.2, zaq-emb.30.3, zaq-emb.30.4, zaq-emb.30.5.

# #768 — PR B first leg: Person-bound authorized execution

Updated: 2026-10-07. Status: implementation proposal, ready for Build mode;
aligned to `a0c8796e`; current PR A CI completion remains a separate landing gate.
Tracking: `zaq-emb.30`, within outcome PR B (`zaq-emb.28`).

This updates the first-leg plan through the coverage and edge-case fixes following
`955bf4e0`, retaining the earlier `73df6235` remediation. Start the whole first leg
from the latest inspected PR A base, preserving ownership, performance, timeout,
conversation-binding and missing-root contracts. The former
side-session wait remains removed. Materialize the work packages below in Beadwork
after switching to Build; this update changes planning files only.

## 1. Verified baseline and delivery

- PR A: #835, branch `feature/issue-768-history-a-integration`.
- Verified local HEAD, remote-tracking branch and GitHub PR head:
  `a0c8796e21412a4e4334d4bd5ee928d339638c78`. Checkout clean at inspection.
- The previously in-flight test work is now committed in `941c8536`, with follow-up
  regressions/fixes in `a0c8796e`. Both are included in this base. Remove that test
  handoff wait; review and extend the committed tests rather than duplicating them.
- Current CI snapshot: **10 of 12 reported checks passed**; Firefox and WebKit are
  in progress, with no completed failure reported. Chromium, native Postgres,
  ParadeDB, optional Elixir 1.20 and the reported quality/security checks passed.
  The aggregate User Journeys QA result has not yet appeared in this snapshot.
  [Current E2E run](https://github.com/www-zaq-ai/zaq/actions/runs/37676651944),
  [current Elixir CI](https://github.com/www-zaq-ai/zaq/actions/runs/37676651898).
- Historical Firefox result on `955bf4e0`: 143 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed at
  `test/e2e/specs/system_config.spec.js:299`, "flash auto-dismisses without user
  interaction": `LLM settings saved.` remained visible after the 10-second wait.
  This is prior-run evidence, not a current-head failure or a diagnosed cause.
  Neither of the new commits edits that browser assertion. Check the current run
  before deciding whether an owning-PR follow-up is still needed; do not weaken it.
- The old all-green result applies only to `73df6235`. The scoped remediation
  re-review predates these later commits; this planning impact assessment is not a
  replacement full code review. Local validation follow-ups `zaq-mcw` (telemetry
  sandbox checkout) and `zaq-e8q` (OAuth/profile validation deadlocks) remain open
  in Beadwork. Reconcile their evidence with the now-passing CI test matrix in
  Build rather than silently closing them or repeating old local pass claims.
- PR B development can proceed from the published base. Reconcile current browser
  and aggregate QA results before landing; fix any confirmed base issue on PR A
  and propagate it into B. Coverage detail and final human acceptance remain
  separate from published-code availability.
- In Build, create `feature/issue-768-history-b-execution` in the user-approved
  isolated worktree from this PR A branch, requiring the verified commit in its
  ancestry. If the base advances, inspect its delta before using the newer tip.
- PR B targets `feature/issue-768-history-a-integration` while stacked. Keep the
  existing two-outcome delivery contract: this is the first implementation leg
  on B's branch, not a new PR per work package or a claim that all B is complete.
- Move this session to the new worktree; use branch-isolated databases and build
  outputs. Follow the worktree setup skill with PR A as the explicit start ref,
  rather than the skill's default `main` start ref.

Authoritative remediation evidence:

- `docs/exec-plans/active/2026-10-01-handoff-channel-boundaries.md`, especially
  Communication boundary and public contracts / Preserved remediation.
- `docs/exec-plans/review/2026-10-04-pr835-remediation-finalization.md`.
- `zaq-emb.27.28.6` publication comment and the actual committed source.
- `docs/services/message-lifecycle.md` for the current incoming/passive/response
  and outgoing-confirmation paths; keep its sequence diagrams in sync with B.
- Post-remediation commits `108abbd8`, `8e99ad7d`, `b7fc95a3`, `955bf4e0` and
  the current contracts/tests. `zaq-7uz` and `zaq-cnt` record the later publications.
- Committed coverage `941c8536` and edge-case correction `a0c8796e`; the latter
  changes only TranscriptHistory, ChannelHistoryProjection and associated tests.
- [Latest plan alignment review](768-history-b-first-leg-review.md).

Older handoff statements that commits or CI are pending are historical. Reconcile
tracking with verified evidence in Build; do not close PR A approval gates merely
because its implementation is available.

### Impact of the newly inspected commits

| Commit | Delivered change | Remaining-work impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `108abbd8` | Ecto-based batched participant projection, deterministic ties/merged-Person deduplication, removal of Audience's 100-recipient/101-metadata-entry caps, lifecycle documentation | B2/B4 preserve the complete message-local audience and distinguish observed participants from membership/authorization. Model-context limits must not truncate capture evidence. |
| `8e99ad7d` | PersonMerger coordinates history ownership through narrow Conversations context APIs; old `plan_person_merge`/`apply_person_merge` helpers removed | B2/B3 use literal-owner reads and validated updates; history discovery and access still require permission-aware APIs. Preserve merge atomicity and distinct replica resources. |
| `b7fc95a3` | Reused capture/admission/confirmation reads, selected-connector reuse, coalesced date-aware accounting; SearchKnowledgeBase declares 120-second tool budget | B1–B4 retain query budgets, lock/transaction boundaries, accounting semantics and tool budgets. These optimizations do not implement canonical hydration or request correlation. |
| `955bf4e0` | Factory timeout regression/property coverage updated for the Search declaration and live tool removal | Reuse these tests during B1 and later timeout work; keep declaration maximum, default floor and registration-order invariants. |
| `941c8536` | Broad channel/history/routing coverage, including Agent binding, runtime-error, persistence-failure and delivery tests | The former in-flight coverage is now available in B's base. Preserve its unique assertions; tests with internal stubs remain focused regressions, not substitutes for B4's real production-path test. |
| `a0c8796e` | Conversation-less execution-message reuse fails closed; batched root ratings ignore nil/duplicate root IDs; missing-root threads remain visible/readable | B2/B3 must retain trusted conversation-backed execution reuse and avoid arbitrary ID adoption. B2/B4 and `.5` must tolerate an absent root without inventing content, losing replies or corrupting cursors/ratings. |

The core first-leg gaps remain verified: Executor still discards `request` from
`ask_with_config`, StreamEvents derives its registry ID from incoming metadata,
and HistoryLoader's conversation path still reads legacy `Message.conversation_id`.
`.30`, `.5`, `.16` and `.7` remain open; `.8` remains in progress. No task is marked
complete merely because its foundations changed. The latest two commits do not
change the core runtime files or ExecutionRecord schema. No migration was added
by these later commits; retain the existing source-account-key migration in the base.

## 2. Remediation contracts this leg must preserve

The original remediation proposal was superseded during implementation. Consume
the final contracts, not its intermediate HistoryEvidence/HistoryProvider design.

| Area | Current contract and consequence for B |
| --- | --- |
| Normalized ingress | `Incoming.RoutingContext.conversation_type` is `:one_to_one`, `:room`, `:recipient_addressed`, or nil. Channels owns provider parsing, exact source scope, timestamps and message-local audience. Do not restore `history_kind` or `title_style` transport fields. |
| Policy/capture | `Engine.History.CommunicationPolicy.kind/1` maps neutral facts to Direct/Shared/Replicated; Engine derives titles and capture policy. Reuse normal ingress and `IncomingMessageRouter`; do not restore caller-controlled `capture_history` flags or provider branches in Agent/Engine. |
| Source identity | `SourceIdentity.valid_scope?/1` accepts nil or an opaque 1–255-byte binary. Preserve JSON account-key encoding and canonical identity. Apply `20261003000000_widen_message_source_account_key.exs`; it widens storage to text without rewriting data, and refuses unsafe rollback narrowing. |
| Replay/merge | Conflicting placement/audience fails rather than adopting old replicas. Preserve canonical UUIDs, positions, separate replica resources and post-merge replay behavior. Redelivery never recreates revoked grants. |
| Conversation-less canonical rows | They remain valid canonical content, but `existing_message_id` reuse as an admitted input or confirmed execution response requires the existing conversation-backed proof. A nil conversation returns `:source_conflict` with no row/placement/cursor mutation; do not treat arbitrary canonical IDs as execution capabilities. |
| Delivery | Channels `DeliveryConfirmation.record/3` dispatches neutral receipt/outgoing evidence via Engine `:record_delivery_confirmation`. `Engine.History.Delivery` interprets it and delegates canonical confirmation to `HistoryIngress`. A successful send with unavailable association stays a successful send; no resend through history recovery. |
| Configuration | The schema is `Zaq.Engine.ChannelConfig`, retaining its existing table and IDs. Email persistence/archive policy are Engine-owned; transport receives supplied runtime maps. B fixtures and aliases must follow the moved schema. |
| Provider queries/BO | Room capability/member/message queries are consumer-neutral. Preserve batched BO projections, detail-only provider root fallback, confidential administration and runtime-only archive retry. |
| Missing thread roots | A child transcript and its authorized replies remain usable when no local root exists. Root projection is nullable; mixed pages preserve order, titles and existing root ratings, and rating lookup filters nil/duplicate IDs. BO detail may use its existing authorized provider fallback; Agent hydration must not borrow that admin privilege or invent a root. |
| Ownership APIs | `Conversations.list_owned_transcripts/2`, `list_person_executions/2`, `change_transcript_owner/2`, `update_transcript_owner/2`, `change_execution_owner/2`, `update_execution_owner/2` replace merge-specific context helpers. Reads use literal owners and stable ID order. `lock: true` requires an existing transaction; `allow_missing_table: true` is historical-migration compatibility only, never a live-history error fallback. These are internal storage APIs, not authorization grants. |
| Capture/admission performance | Reuse the connector and canonical message within one capture's recipient fan-out; still validate each target and lock association writes. Admission reuses its validated source result under the existing source lock. Do not hoist these values into cross-request caches or bypass fresh permission checks. |
| Confirmation input | `TranscriptHistory.prepare_execution_response/3` now receives the already-locked response `%Message{}` as its second argument, not an answer ID to reload. Only the enclosing HistoryIngress confirmation transaction supplies that row; preserve pair/source checks and durable recovery. |
| Transport selection | Provider-only delivery/upsert resolves the connector once and calls `fetch_connection_details_for_config/1` on that exact row. Preserve explicit-connector and ambiguity behavior when changing request/status/delivery paths. |
| Accounting | Pending usage jobs coalesce by conversation/model/date only in available/scheduled/retryable states. Executing jobs must allow a later pass. Aggregation locks conversation metadata and sums the explicit message day using a half-open UTC interval; retries replace totals rather than incrementing twice. |
| Tool budgets | SearchKnowledgeBase declares 120,000 ms; effective Jido worker budget is the maximum declared by enabled tools with the ordinary 15,000-ms floor. Preserve live add/remove behavior and the distinction between tool execution, stream inactivity, request wait and delivery deadlines. |

Admission/finalization remain the existing Engine operations. Preserve the current
binding's `conversation_id`, `user_message_id` and opaque `finalization_token` while
adding validated execution references as necessary; update every consumer of any
intentional extension. A message ID or caller-supplied binding is not authority.

## 3. Implementation sequence — regressions before each change

### B0 — workspace, baseline and tracking

- Read applicable Agent harness checks, Engine guide, Action reuse, testing and
  workflow policies, plus `docs/services/message-lifecycle.md`. Verify existing
  moduledocs and callers before extending them. Serena returned empty overviews
  for the inspected Engine modules; bounded source reads supplied this assessment.
- Verify effective Repo host/port/database before setup or migrations. The latest
  dev configuration adds DB_PORT/DB_NAME handling but contains two database
  entries; do not assume an environment override provides worktree isolation.
- Create/reuse child issues under `.30` for B1–B4, wire dependencies, and verify the
  ready set. Keep full-outcome approval/E2E issues separate from this first leg.
- Record B3's concrete receipt/state-transition representation and canonical usage
  source as a bounded contract-design subtask. Resolve both against the existing
  schema, constraints and consumers before B1–B3 production changes; its output is
  the field/result contract and failing tests, not a new execution subsystem.
  The acceptance invariants in B3 are fixed; physical storage must honor them.
- Start from `a0c8796e`, which already contains the former test handoff. Review the
  now-committed Agent API/executor, delivery, transcript and projection regressions
  before editing overlapping tests. Recheck for any newer user/session work at
  Build startup and preserve it; no additional handoff is currently required.
- Run targeted baseline regressions for source identity/storage, replay/merge,
  neutral ingress/delivery and the existing real Mattermost history flow in the
  isolated worktree. Reuse existing tests; do not recreate remediation tests.
- Include the newly added ownership, audience/projection, query-budget, accounting
  and Factory timeout tests listed in B4, plus conversation-less reuse and missing-
  root regressions. Reconcile the current CI run rather than carrying forward the
  previous head's failed or passing status as current acceptance evidence.
- Author the primary full-path scenario specified in B4 now and confirm its
  missing-behavior failures before B1–B3 production changes. Keep it as the
  acceptance test throughout implementation; B4 completes the matrix and validates
  the integrated result rather than postponing that first regression.
- Action reuse: setup/tracking is not an executable domain operation. Record
  baseline results in Beadwork, not as new repository policy documentation.

### B1 — actual request identity and runtime lifecycle

**Owners:** `RequestRegistry`, `Executor`, `StreamEvents`, `Factory`, `ServerManager`.

Tests first: real Jido handle versus external correlation ID; simultaneous requests;
busy/finalizing rejection retaining a healthy runtime; stale event/control/cleanup
against a replacement incarnation; scope/owner collision isolation.

Implementation:

- Retain Jido's returned request handle instead of discarding it. Register the
  actual request ID with exact runtime PID/incarnation, owning node, actor and
  execution scope; keep external correlation separately.
- Make ownership updates atomic and fence stale/terminal updates. Reuse existing
  request inspection and stop-if-current lifecycle mechanisms.
- Distinguish ordinary admission rejection from execution failure; a rejected
  second request must not stop or overwrite the active request.
- Keep registry/control data bounded and private. Preserve existing configured-
  agent credential binding and provider-independent Factory execution.
- Preserve the configured tool-budget pipeline while passing the actual request
  handle. Run `factory_test.exs` and `factory_tool_timeout_test.exs`, including
  reverse/deduplicated registration and live removal from 120,000 to 90,000 to
  15,000 ms. Use barriers to exercise long-running tool lifecycle/heartbeat
  behavior; tests need not sleep for production-length budgets.
- Retain `941c8536` regressions for atom/string-key binding equivalence, unavailable
  runtime lookups, handled cleanup exits and reusable busy failures. If B's new
  Person-bound runtime key intentionally changes an exact-name expectation,
  replace that representation assertion with evidence of the same binding
  semantics plus Person/connector isolation; never weaken the behavior assertion.

Action reuse: extend the existing lifecycle APIs; registry bookkeeping is local
runtime infrastructure, not a new workflow Action or exposed agent tool.
Mocking: local LLM HTTP endpoint only; real Jido/processes, barrier synchronization.
Documentation: affected API/module contracts and `docs/services/agent.md`.

### B2 — trusted admission and authorized initial history

**Owners:** `IncomingMessageRouter`, Engine conversation/history APIs, Agent API,
`HistoryLoader`, existing `accounts.fetch_history` Action.

Tests first: missing/forged/conflicting actors; nonexistent Person; revoked grants;
cross-connector collisions; two People sharing a transcript; BO session identity;
authorized Direct/Shared/Replicated hydration; available-root deduplication;
missing/deleted root with retained replies; bounded parent history, sibling
exclusion and private-data exclusion.

Implementation:

- Resolve Person, canonical input and transcript through trusted ingress and the
  remediated placement contract. Keep identity/authorization in their owning domains.
- Preserve the nil-conversation reuse guards. Actual pre-captured external input
  enters through Engine admission, which establishes its verified execution
  binding; Agent code and fixtures must not fill a missing conversation ID or
  manufacture execution provenance. Canonical capture/read without a legacy
  conversation remains valid and is distinct from that privileged reuse path.
- Reuse the current source-lock/validated-source flow rather than restoring
  repeated connector or canonical-message lookups. Preserve the unscoped admission
  post-insert side-effect boundary covered by its regression; isolate any new
  Person execution transaction rather than wrapping legacy delivery/title work.
- Reuse `Permissions`, strategy context-source rules and sanitized canonical read
  APIs. Add a fixed Engine dispatch operation only where the existing role API
  lacks the required authorized projection; it delegates to the same domain read.
- Keep DB/policy projection in Engine and conversion to Jido context in Agent.
  Reuse the history Action's authorization semantics; do not create a second
  history tool or use its legacy broad query as an authorization shortcut.
- Include passive/failed incoming messages as factual history; exclude the current
  input from hydration when Jido will append it. Deduplicate by canonical UUID.
- Include a retained authorized root at most once. If the root is unavailable,
  continue with authorized thread replies and bounded parent background; preserve
  their order and IDs without a synthetic root or new provider request. Model
  hydration does not use BO's super-admin detail/root-fetch operation.
- Preserve all valid Audience recipients/participant metadata, including inputs
  above the former caps. Apply model/history-page limits to authorized projections,
  not to recipient placement evidence. Observed-participant previews and literal
  ownership lists must never stand in for grants or a provider membership roster.
- Validate access on each explicit request, including warm reuse. Failed canonical
  authorization never falls back to unfiltered legacy history or permission bypass.
- Preserve existing explicit BO/system paths and private legacy access contracts;
  nil Person does not acquire channel-history access.
- Keep bounded projection queries explicit. Existing query reuse is scoped to a
  single operation/transaction, not proof that cached authorization is reusable on
  a later request, internal turn or after Person/grant changes.

Action reuse: extend existing admission and history operations; execution hydration
is an internal lifecycle consumer. Reads use existing NodeRouter domain boundaries.
Mocking: provider/LLM edges only; permissions, routing and persistence stay real.
Documentation: Agent/Engine service contracts and affected public API moduledocs.

### B3 — private outcomes and explicit busy/steering disposition

**Owners:** Engine admission/finalization and `ExecutionRecord`, Agent API/runtime
control, StreamEvents. Consume B1 identity and B2 authorized bindings.

Tests first: finalization replay/concurrency; invalid capability and actor; one
public-answer owner; same-Person steering; cross-Person control denial; queued input
followed by failure/sealing/overflow; stale handle; failed persistence; LLM/tool
failure; delivery failure after successful execution.

Preserve conversation-less user/assistant rejection with the existing message
unchanged, zero new placements and unchanged transcript position. Preserve the
new Agent API tests proving persistence failure blocks delivery and error logs
exclude sensitive changeset/exception/map details.

Implementation:

- Wire new Person-bound execution ownership, capability hash, private trace/tool
  results, usage and outcomes through `ExecutionRecord`. Preserve legacy references
  and artifact access; do not repair old data or duplicate private data in new
  shareable projections. Finalization is atomic/idempotent against the same UUIDs.
- Retain the conversation-backed execution pair while wiring ExecutionRecord in
  this leg. Its introduction must not relax the new nil-conversation source-conflict
  checks; canonical-only execution without that binding would require a separately
  designed replacement proof, not deletion of a rejection guard.
- Keep ownership transfers inside PersonMerger's transaction through the current
  Conversations read/change/update APIs. Preserve resource IDs, placements,
  capability/message references and rollback; do not restore the removed merge
  helpers or add direct schema persistence to Accounts.
- Account for the existing worker when moving usage into execution-private storage:
  it currently sums assistant Message fields. Define the canonical accounting
  source before cutover and adapt that same worker if needed, preserving legacy
  totals and counting each finalized answer once. Test mixed legacy/new records,
  replay, failed/steered inputs, concurrent models, delayed message dates and an
  input arriving while accounting executes. Private-storage separation must not
  silently zero totals, double-count usage, or introduce a second accounting job.
- Inspect/steer/inject must validate trusted actor and exact active request scope,
  not possession of a registry key. Carry the actual Jido handle to Factory.
- Same-Person explicit inputs may steer that execution; another Person's input
  retains its own ownership. Background messages do not become steering authority.
- Distinguish queued, consumed and terminal-unconsumed input. Use Jido's existing
  `input_injected` event/canonical references to confirm consumption; its queued
  acknowledgement alone does not establish that a request was answered.
- Keep one root execution/public-answer owner and private per-input disposition.
  Use the minimal representation selected in B0 against the existing schema:
  `completed` currently requires a unique public answer, so do not mark a
  second steered execution completed against that same answer. Record the concrete
  receipt/schema decision in its issue; any required DDL is a forward migration
  with fresh/populated-path tests. Do not add a durable queue/crash-recovery system.
- Busy/finalizing inputs receive an explicit result. Unconsumed inputs remain
  factual history with unsuccessful/unconsumed disposition, never a false answer.
- Preserve execution-persisted versus delivery-confirmed results using the new
  Engine delivery boundary. Association recovery never repeats the provider send.
- Carry the locked response row through confirmation preparation and retain the
  exact selected connector for status/delivery; no answer reload or provider-only
  re-resolution after selection. Distinguish these bounded reuse contracts from
  any new execution-record reads, which need their own explicit budget.

Action reuse: extend existing finalize/control operations; no parallel execution
Action or response builder. Mocking: only external HTTP edges; race tests use real
processes and DB locking/events, with no production-only test switches or sleeps.
Documentation: Agent/Engine lifecycle, result shapes and any migration contract.

### B4 — complete full-path acceptance and regression preservation

Extend `test/zaq/channels/mattermost_shared_history_integration_test.exs` and its
existing support fixtures (or a focused companion) with a real configured Jido
agent and registered tool. Use the remediated provider registration, neutral facts
and Engine configuration schema. Keep NodeRouter, permission checks, Engine,
Factory, Jido and tool implementation real; fake only provider HTTP and LLM APIs.

The primary scenario must:

1. Create two People, a connector, routing rule and real grants.
2. Establish passive/shared/thread history through real provider ingress; create
   distinguishable forbidden history and another execution's private data.
3. Send an explicit request through the actual chat adapter and normal route.
4. Inspect the actual LLM request: authorized attributed history present, root and
   current input once when the root exists, forbidden/private data absent; the
   missing-root companion includes the current input once and preserves replies.
5. Return a tool call, execute a real registered tool, inspect the correctly paired
   tool result in the next LLM request, then return the final answer.
6. Assert Person/runtime/request ownership, private persistence, one public-answer
   UUID, exact connector/channel/thread delivery and confirmed canonical placement.
7. Replay the input and verify no second execution, answer, placement or delivery.

Companion scenarios cover B1–B3 races/failures and Direct/Replicated authorization,
including remediated long scopes, conflicting replay, merged replica isolation,
conversation-less execution reuse rejection and missing-root hydration. For the
last case, inspect the actual LLM request and ensure no fabricated root or
unauthorized provider/admin fetch occurs; BO rendering tests alone are insufficient.
Property tests cover broad isolation/idempotency/state-transition invariants, not
implementation mirroring. Preserve unique coverage while removing obsolete paths.

Preservation matrix for the October 7 base (run affected suites, extend only for
new behavior):

- `test/zaq/accounts/person_merge_test.exs`: narrow ownership APIs, ordered
  transaction locks, validation/rollback and migration-only missing-table handling.
- `test/zaq/engine/messages/incoming/audience_test.exs` and
  `test/zaq/engine/channel_history_admin_test.exs`: complete audience evidence,
  participant tie ordering, merged-Person deduplication and assistant exclusion.
- `test/zaq/engine/conversations/transcript_history_test.exs`: five recipient
  placements share one canonical message insert and one connector lookup; recipient
  reordering/duplicates preserve message identity and transcript positions;
  conversation-less user/assistant reuse rejects atomically without modifying
  the canonical message or transcript position.
- `test/zaq/engine/channel_history_projection_test.exs` and
  `test/zaq_web/live/bo/communication/channel_history_live_test.exs`: missing-root
  child visibility/readability and mixed-page order/rating preservation, including
  the authorized detail provider-404 case. Preserve batched root/rating lookup.
- `test/zaq/engine/history_ingress_test.exs`: scoped admission has one connector
  lookup; confirmation has two Message SELECTs, reuses the locked answer and keeps
  replay identity; unscoped message insertion retains its side-effect boundary.
- `test/zaq/channels/api_test.exs`: provider-only status selection loads one
  connector and derives connection details from that same row.
- `test/zaq/engine/conversations/token_usage_aggregator_test.exs`: pending coalescing,
  executing-job follow-up, retry-safe totals, explicit date and concurrent-model locks.
- `test/zaq/agent/factory_test.exs` and `factory_tool_timeout_test.exs`: declared
  maximum, default floor, effective worker configuration and live removal.
- `test/zaq/agent/api_test.exs`, `executor_test.exs` and
  `executor_integration_test.exs`: committed malformed-input/binding/runtime/error-
  sanitization/telemetry coverage. Preserve those focused contracts while adding
  real-Jido ownership and race tests rather than counting internal stub coverage
  as proof of B4's external-edges-only flow.
- The committed delivery-confirmation, Engine history-delivery/recovery and
  conversation-identity suites cover failure/retry scopes. Reuse them for B3/.8;
  do not recreate a second confirmation fixture or recovery implementation.
  Concrete paths: `test/zaq/channels/delivery_confirmation_test.exs`,
  `test/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge/delivery_result_test.exs`,
  `test/zaq/engine/history/delivery_test.exs`,
  `test/zaq/engine/history_delivery_worker_test.exs` and
  `test/zaq/engine/messages/conversation_identity_test.exs`.

Reuse `Zaq.QueryRecorder` for synchronous domain-query budgets; it records only the
calling process, so it cannot prove the full asynchronous/Jido flow's query count.
Keep those budgets alongside the real full-flow test. Placement work may grow with
recipient count; shared message/connector resolution must not. Budget legitimate
new execution/hydration queries separately rather than weakening existing assertions.

Use explicit endpoint barriers, events, monitored shutdown and sandbox ownership.
Do not accept arbitrary `_request` LLM payloads or blanket-stub internal dispatch.
If shared application configuration is unavoidable, isolate that suite and restore
state; prefer existing per-boundary configuration and ephemeral ports.

Action reuse: verification only; exercise the same production APIs. Document fixture
purpose and record commands/results in Beadwork. These ExUnit integration tests are
immediate regression protection; browser feature E2E retains its human gate.

## 4. Effects on the later remaining tasks

| Task | Carry-forward requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `.5` fixed-cursor per-turn refresh | Batch bounded authorized reads per transcript/source and test query growth across internal turns. Keep one cursor per association stream; cached capture validation is not read authorization. Complete recipient evidence survives model-budget trimming; original/steered input and tool pairs stay deduplicated.
